I never went to school, can't read or write, but I've been farming these fields for twenty years and I know what I'm doing. I got about 350 mu here in Quzhou, way too much for just my family of four to handle. My wife and I work the farm full-time, and our two kids help when they're not busy. Everything else I hire out — workers for planting and digging, tractors for plowing, machines for the corn harvest.

This year I'm putting 200 mu in corn, 80 mu in sweet potatoes, and the rest — about 70 mu — in millet. Corn is easy with machines and the grain buyer drives right to the edge of my field. Sweet potatoes earn decent money but I can't plant too many because finding workers to stick the slips and dig them up is hard and getting more expensive every year. Millet is my safe crop — cheap to grow, doesn't need much water or labor, and the dealer always takes it.

For the corn, I'll plant in early May with hybrid seed. I buy fresh seed every year — learned long ago that saved hybrid seed grows poorly. Costs me about 50 yuan per mu. At planting I spread about half a bag of that compound fertilizer per mu — the kind with the three numbers, about 25 kg worth. Then when the corn is knee-high, around late June, I topdress with another 15 kg of urea. I irrigate three times from the well: once right after planting if the rain doesn't come, once when it's shooting up, and once when the grain is filling. Well water isn't free — I pay for the diesel to pump it — so I don't waste it. I spray herbicide once and if I see corn borers I spray insecticide too. With the machines doing most of the work, my family mainly oversees things, but I still hire about a hundred days of labor for tasks the machines miss. I expect around 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

Sweet potatoes go in late May. I use my own slips from last year's crop and buy some to fill the gap, costs about 40 yuan per mu. They like that potassium fertilizer, so I put down about 30 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting — all at once, no topdressing. I irrigate twice if it's dry. The real headache is labor — planting the slips by hand, weeding between the ridges, and then digging them up in October. I hire nearly all of it, probably four hundred days of hired labor across the season. I expect about 1,800 kg of tubers per mu. I spray herbicide but usually don't need much else.

Millet is simple. I plant in mid-May with local seed, about 25 yuan per mu. One application of fertilizer at planting, about 20 kg of compound per mu. Maybe irrigate once if the spring is dry. Harvest in late September. Hardly any pesticides. Mostly machine work, just a little hired help. Should get around 220 kg per mu.

I plow all the fields in spring with rented tractors. Between the corn, sweet potatoes, and millet, I'm looking at about 110,000 yuan in total input costs this year — seed, fertilizer, hired labor, diesel for pumping, and chemicals. That's a lot of money to put out, but corn and sweet potatoes usually pay it back. I'm not trying anything new this year — last year was decent, so I'll stick with what I know. Change is risky when you've got this much land and this much money on the line.
